gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-mono: Stencilia is a structural display face with spacious gaps at its curve terminals, and Noto Sans Mono sits beneath it, sturdy and generously spaced. Long paragraphs would move steadily along.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-multan: Noto Sans Multani reads modern and lofty, its e left wide open. Stencilia is best at striking, structural headings with spacious terminal gaps, while the body font is best at quietly carrying the text beneath.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-nandin: Striking up top, approachable below, with short ascenders and a big lowercase body underneath Stencilia's structural display letters. And Noto Sans Nandinagari keeps its openings generous at every weight, which is the real strength of this pairing.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu holds its terminals far from the stroke body and stands on a towering x-height, modern and contemporary throughout. Stencilia brings the structural display punch above it.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Structural and striking, then clean and tall: Stencilia heads the pair with real presence. Noto Sans Ogham brings wide gaps in the e and lowercase that looks bold because its bodies stand so tall, which is the strongest quality here.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-sc: Chalky curves that stop short of closing, set under Stencilia's striking display. Noto Sans SC keeps its ascenders barely above the x-height, so a long passage would read low, modern and unhurried.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-siddha: Noto Sans Siddham reads approachable and contemporary, with a large central band in the text line and an s whose ends hang far from the spine. Under Stencilia's structural display heading, a long passage would feel open and easygoing.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le reads neutral and approachable, its ink strokes tapering out before they touch, with hardly any step from capital to lowercase. Stencilia's structural display letters feel bolder beside it.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-tamil-: Spacious gaps at the curve terminals make Stencilia look structural and striking, a display face built to grab attention. But Noto Sans Tamil Supplement does the quieter work, with round forms like open parentheses and a middle band so tall the line looks stocky.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Striking, structural display letters over a quiet text face. Stencilia is best at grabbing attention with its spacious terminal gaps, while Noto Sans Telugu is best at staying professional, with a high-set midline and counters that connect to the outside.
